target.description: Histidine catabolism disposes of surplus dietary histidine and connects it to glutamate and one-carbon metabolism. target.description: post-chaperonin tubulin folding pathway finishes the job of making usable tubulin: after the CCT chaperonin releases partially folded alpha- and beta-tubulin, a set of dedicated cofactors completes folding and assembles the two into the heterodimer that microtubules are built from. target.name: behavioral response to nicotine
target.description: Nicotine changes behaviour because it hijacks the neuronal nicotinic acetylcholine receptors that normally tune dopamine and other transmitter release in reward circuitry; the behavioural response to nicotine is the locomotor, reinforcing and aversive output of that action, and it underlies tolerance, self-administration and dependence in smokers. The receptor subunits here assemble into pentamers with distinct pharmacology: alpha4-beta2 combinations mediate high-affinity nicotine binding and reward in the ventral tegmental area, alpha6-containing receptors act on striatal dopamine terminals, and the alpha5/alpha3/beta4 cluster in the medial habenula sets the aversive, intake-limiting arm, with human variants in that cluster among the strongest genetic risks for heavy smoking.

target.name: Defective SLC26A3 causes congenital secretory chloride diarrhea 1 (DIAR1)
target.description: Absorption of salt and water by the intestine depends on an apical chloride/bicarbonate exchanger in the colon and ileum, and loss of that exchanger is the basis of congenital secretory chloride diarrhea. target.name: positive regulation of enamel mineralization
target.description: Tooth enamel is the hardest tissue in the body, and it reaches that state only when ameloblasts drive the ordered deposition of calcium phosphate into a protein scaffold; this pathway covers the processes that promote enamel mineralization. Enamelin and the amelotin and ODAPH proteins of the ameloblast secretory and maturation stages organize crystal growth and the attachment of cells to the mineralizing front, while ion transport across the ameloblast membrane keeps the extracellular environment permissive: the anion channel CFTR and the anion exchanger SLC4A2 handle chloride and bicarbonate movement that buffers the protons released as hydroxyapatite forms.
